title: The PRISMA 2020 statement: an updated guideline for reporting systematic reviews
extended_summary:
This paper presents PRISMA 2020, an updated reporting guideline for systematic reviews. The authors address the problem that the original 2009 PRISMA statement no longer fully reflected advances in systematic review methods, terminology, and publishing practices. The paper’s purpose is to provide updated guidance so that authors can more transparently and completely report why a review was done, how studies were identified and synthesised, and what was found.

The approach studied is the development and presentation of a reporting framework rather than an educational or clinical intervention. PRISMA 2020 includes a revised 27-item checklist, an abstract checklist, an expanded checklist, and updated flow diagrams. The guideline was developed through literature reviews of reporting problems and existing guidance, a survey of systematic review methodologists and journal editors, an in-person consensus meeting, and multiple rounds of author feedback and revision.

The paper does not study students, teachers, or schools as participants, and it is not focused on writing instruction or feedback interventions. Instead, it is aimed at authors, editors, peer reviewers, and users of systematic reviews across fields, including health, social, and educational interventions. The context is scholarly research reporting, with contributors and authors drawn from multiple countries and institutions.

The main conclusion is that PRISMA 2020 replaces PRISMA 2009 and should be used to improve the transparency, completeness, and accuracy of systematic review reporting. The authors argue that better reporting will help readers judge trustworthiness, facilitate replication and updating, reduce research waste, and support evidence-based decision making. The paper is therefore best understood as a methodological guidance document, not as evidence about comparator conditions or writing-feedback practices in secondary education.
quality_tier_rationale: This paper is a reporting-guideline/methods statement for systematic reviews (PRISMA 2020), not an empirical study or evidence synthesis about writing instruction interventions. It does not evaluate any educational intervention, comparator, or student outcome.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports no intervention effects on student writing or any K-12 educational outcomes, so there is no measurable instructional impact to assign.
